documents.title: Home blood pressure
documents.author: patient
documents.body: We bought a cuff at the drugstore. My readings in the morning are about 128-136 over 78-84. Is that OK or should I be lower? - Gene

documents.title: RE: Home blood pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those are good numbers, Gene. Keep doing what you're doing. Bring the cuff to your March visit and we'll check it against ours.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Brought home cuff - reads within 4 points of ours. Winter was quiet. Still swimming. Shingrix: Part D covers it, he'll go to the pharmacy.
O: BP per flowsheet. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact. R arm rigidity mild, unchanged; walks briskly.
A/P: HTN controlled. T2DM - A1c today. CKD 3a - creatinine today. Continue all. RTC 6 mo for AWV, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c and kidney numbers are right where they have been. Potassium normal. No changes for now.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No show for 9:30. Called home, wife answered - they were at the lake and forgot. Will roll this into his September wellness visit.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV. Missed August f/u, covering chronic issues today too.
HRA: independent, drives, no falls, hearing ok. Wife handles the calendar, he still does the checkbook.
Mini-Cog normal. PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: still none on file; he says he 'keeps meaning to.' Re-offered the form.
Vaccines: Shingrix series complete (3/22, 6/22). PCV20 and high-dose flu today. Bivalent covid booster at pharmacy.
Exam: weight stable. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: intact monofilament, pulses 2+. Mild R arm cogwheeling, no tremor, gait normal.
A/P: HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a, HLD stable - annual labs. BPH stable. PD stable, no treatment. RTC 4-5 months.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of this year's labs look like last year's - sugar control good, kidney function stable, cholesterol fine on atorvastatin, urine protein normal.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Exam date 11/8/2022. VA 20/25 OD, 20/30 OS. Pseudophakia OU, capsules clear. Dilated fundus exam without retinopathy or edema. Glasses Rx updated. Annual follow-up. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came alone. Says he is fine, quieter winter, less swimming since the pool hours changed. No complaints offered. Meds unchanged, no misses.
Exam: vitals ok. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Ext without edema. R arm rigidity as before.
Plan: labs. Continue meds. RTC summer.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Gene - A1c is fine. Kidney function is a touch lower than last year, still in the same stage. Keep up fluids, no ibuprofen or naproxen. We'll recheck in the summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.reason: progressive gait change, cognitive change, urinary urgency, falls

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife, who asked for this visit.
HPI: Since around January she has noticed he walks slower and his feet seem to stick, takes small steps. Fell twice in the last month - once in the garage, once getting up from the couch - no head strike, no LOC, no injury. Repeating himself, misplacing things. Has to rush to the bathroom and has wet himself a few times. He minimizes all of it, 'just getting old.'
Exam: vitals ok. Alert, oriented, but slow to answer. Heart regular, lungs clear. Gait: wide, slow, short steps, feet barely clear the floor, turns in several steps. Rigidity both legs more than arms. No focal weakness.
A/P: Subacute gait decline with cognitive change and urgency in a man with known mild PD. This is more than his PD has looked like. Neurology referral, asked for a prompt slot. Home safety reviewed - remove throw rugs, night lights, grab bar. Labs today. Wife to call with any further fall.

documents.title: Neurology referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referring Eugene Holt, 72, for evaluation of about 5 months of progressive gait difficulty with two recent falls, new memory complaints and urinary urgency with incontinence. History of mild Parkinson disease (outside neurology 2019, untreated), HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a, BPH s/p TURP. Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA. Thank you for seeing him.

documents.title: Neurology appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Neurology office confirmed receipt of referral; appointment 7/17 at 2:00. Wife notified by phone.

events.reason: gait difficulty, memory problems, urinary urgency

reports.text: Technique: axial non-contrast images of the head. Findings: The lateral and third ventricles are enlarged. Cortical sulci show minimal atrophy, less than expected for the ventricular size. No hemorrhage, mass or extra-axial collection. No acute infarct. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium intact. Bilateral lens implants.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged ventricles with minimal cortical atrophy.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology consultation, date of service 7/17/2023.

Reason for referral: gait decline, memory, bladder.

Mr. Holt is a 72-year-old right-handed retired teacher, seen with his wife. Over roughly six months he has had worsening walking, forgetfulness and urinary urgency with occasional incontinence. His wife describes a shuffle and two falls in the past month. He asks the same questions more than once in a conversation.

History: mild Parkinson disease diagnosed 2019, never treated. HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, BPH after TURP 2018. Cataract surgery both eyes 2019, L hernia repair 2010.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother had Lewy body dementia and diabetes; father coronary disease.
Social: former smoker (20 pack-years, quit ~20 years), minimal alcohol.

Examination: Strength full in all four limbs. Tone increased in both lower extremities. Gait broad-based with short, magnetic steps; unable to walk heel-to-toe. 

CT head (today): enlarged ventricles, only minimal cortical atrophy.

Impression: Gait apraxia, cognitive slowing and urge incontinence with ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy - normal pressure hydrocephalus. Background Parkinson disease.

Plan: Follow-up in 3 months with repeat imaging.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Neurology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Gene's wife. The neurologist said he has fluid on the brain, normal pressure something. Did you get the report? What does it mean for him? We are worried.

documents.title: RE: Neurology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, I have the letter and the CT. It's called normal pressure hydrocephalus - the fluid spaces in the brain are larger than they should be, and that can affect walking, memory and the bladder, which fits what you've been seeing. The neurologist plans to see him again in about 3 months with another scan. Happy to go over it in person at his September visit or sooner if you'd like.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, with wife.
Interval: neurology 7/17 - NPH on CT, follow-up with repeat scan in October.
HRA: no falls since June after rugs came up and grab bar went in. Wife now does finances and drives most of the time. Still dresses and bathes himself. Urgency persists, uses pads at night.
Cognitive screen not repeated today, neurology following. PHQ-2 1.
Advance directive: none. Discussed again with both - naming a proxy now while he can choose. Form given; wife to bring it back.
Vaccines: flu and updated covid today. RSV vaccine reviewed, he qualifies; pharmacy.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet intact. Gait wide-based, short steps, slow turns. Leg rigidity.
A/P: NPH and PD - per neurology. HTN, DM, CKD 3a, HLD - annual labs. Fall precautions continue. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from Friday: kidney function a little lower than last year but still in the same range, A1c fine, cholesterol fine. No changes.

reports.text: Comparison 7/17/2023. Non-contrast axial images. The ventricles remain enlarged, similar to the prior study. Sulci are not widened; no cortical atrophy is seen. No hemorrhage, mass effect or extra-axial fluid. No acute territorial infarct.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged ventricles, unchanged. No cortical atrophy.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology follow-up, seen 10/18/2023, accompanied by wife.

Seen in July for gait change. Known Parkinson disease and normal pressure hydrocephalus. Walking has kept getting harder since early this year; he says his feet feel glued to the floor. His wife finds him more forgetful and he sometimes does not reach the toilet in time.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg. NKDA.

Exam: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; fundi without papilledema. Gait broad-based and magnetic with hesitation on starting.

Urinalysis today unremarkable.
Repeat non-contrast CT head: ventricles enlarged as before, no cortical atrophy.

Impression: NPH with gait-predominant picture, background PD.
Plan: Return in about 3 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Seen 11/6/2023 with wife. VA 20/30 OU. IOLs centered. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Advised good lighting at home given recent falls. Recall 1 year. Allergies: NKDA.
